BuildOutput.description:
A single per-platform build output declared in a [`BuildReport`].

Each entry names the platform and a path (relative to `project-dir`)
where the target adapter produced an artifact. The CLI finalize gate
verifies every declared path exists and is non-empty
(`target-build-output-missing`).

path.description: Relative path (from `project-dir`) to the produced artifact.

BuildStatus.description:
Closed build outcome enum.

Partial success is [`BuildStatus::Success`] carrying non-blocking
findings only — the CLI rejects a `success` report with any blocking
finding via the report's internal blocking-findings gate.

oneOf.description: Build succeeded; only non-blocking findings (or none) allowed.

Diagnostic.description:
Structured diagnostic — the neutral currency shared by the validate
and review surfaces.

Producer-local `id` (e.g. `FIND-0001`) is distinct from the codex
`rule_id` (e.g. `UNI-014`): `id` is a stable per-run handle and
`rule_id` is the durable codex citation.

confidence.description:
Producer self-rated confidence. Required for
`source: model-assisted`; the conditional rule is enforced by
the validator, not here.

fingerprint.description:
Stable hash over `(rule-id, location, evidence-payload)`.
Format `sha256:<64 hex chars>`.

id.description: Producer-local stable id for this run (e.g. `FIND-0001`).

kind.description:
Nature axis: defect (`violation`) vs request-for-judgment
(`review`). Defaults to `violation` when the wire field is
omitted.

location.description: Optional anchor location for the diagnostic.

related-rule-ids.description: Additional codex ids that informed the diagnostic.

remediation.description: Concrete action to clear the diagnostic.

rule-id.description:
Rule id (e.g. `UNI-014`); absent for diagnostics that do not
cite codex policy.

slice.description: Slice name when the diagnostic is slice-scoped.

source-adapter.description: Source-adapter name when the diagnostic is source-specific.

target-adapter.description: Target-adapter name when the diagnostic is adapter-specific.

DiagnosticKind.description:
Orthogonal nature axis for a [`Diagnostic`].

Distinguishes a deterministic defect from a deterministically
raised request for judgment. Defaults to [`Self::Violation`] so a
diagnostic that omits the wire field deserialises as a defect, and
so the [`is_blocking`] predicate keeps its pre-axis behaviour.

oneOf.description: A defect: something is wrong and should be fixed. Default.

A request for agent or human judgment raised deterministically
(e.g. a deferred semantic check the producer cannot decide).
Emitted by an external WASI tool (e.g. the contract verifier).

FindingEvidence.description:
Closed evidence union for a [`Diagnostic`].

Internally tagged on `kind` (`deny_unknown_fields` closes each
branch). Producers should keep inline payloads small — reference
large evidence by digest rather than embedding it.

oneOf.description: Bounded verbatim excerpt for local code or prose evidence.
Digest reference for evidence too large or sensitive to inline.

locations.description: Optional contributing locations referenced by the digest.

sha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the underlying evidence bytes.

summary.description: Short human summary of what was hashed.

data.description:
Free-form JSON payload. Producers MUST keep `data` bounded
and secret-free; the validator enforces the 16 `KiB` cap on
the full evidence object.

locations.description: Optional contributing locations referenced by the payload.

FindingLocation.description:
File path plus optional line/column range carried by a
[`Diagnostic`] or by a `digest`/`structured` evidence variant.

end-column.description: Inclusive end column for a multi-line range.

end-line.description: Inclusive end line for a multi-line range.

line.description:
Anchor line (0-indexed; producers commonly emit 1-indexed and
the schema accepts either with `minimum: 0`).

Platform.description:
Target platform for a Specify project.

`Core` is the shared Rust business-logic crate; every project that
declares platforms must include it. The shell variants (`Ios`,
`Android`, `Web`, `Desktop`) represent native presentation layers.

Only `Ios` and `Android` have scaffold/build/verify support today;
`Web` and `Desktop` are type-system placeholders signalling future
functionality.

oneOf.description: Shared Rust business-logic crate (mandatory in every platform set).
Web shell (future — accepted but no build/scaffold support yet).
Desktop shell (future — accepted but no build/scaffold support yet).

Severity.description:
Closed severity enum. Variants are declared in the documented sort
order — the derived [`Ord`] therefore yields `Critical < Important
< Suggestion < Optional`.

```
use diagnostics::Severity;

assert!(Severity::Critical < Severity::Suggestion);
```

oneOf.description: Highest priority; blocks merge in CI.
Should-fix; default escalation level for adapter overlays.

UiSurface.description:
The per-slice "has UI surface" signal authored by the build brief.

Carries the count of screen-bearing requirements the slice
introduces or modifies, derived from the brief's own `spec.md`
judgement (never from `## Platforms`). `screens == 0` means "no UI
surface". The UI-surface coherence check that consumed this signal
lives in-guest (the vectis core's report gate); the engine only
round-trips the field on the wire.

screens.description:
Count of screen-bearing requirements this slice introduces or
modifies. `0` means no UI surface.

description: Generated judgment-answer schema — generated from the Rust wire types by project::answers; do not edit. Validates the schema-gated answer to a target adapter's build or merge operation: the report shape minus the envelope keys (`version`, `slice`, `target`) the caller already knows.

status.description: Operation outcome as judged by the model.

title: Specify build/merge answer
